elements.quote: Our objective was to update the data in a living systematic review of the literature concerning the ef fi cacy and toxicity of the IL-6 receptor antagonist tocilizumab in COVID-19 patients.

elements.quote: Data sources were Ovid MEDLINE(R) and Epub Ahead of Print, In-Process & Other Non-Indexed Citations and Daily, Ovid Embase, Ovid Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Ovid Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, Web of Science, Scopus up, preprint servers and Google from 8th October 2020 till 24th February 2021.

elements.quote: As of October 2020, cumulative moderate-certainty evidence from randomized controlled trials (RCTs) showed that the IL-6 receptor antagonist tocilizumab reduces the risk of mechanical ventilation in hospitalized COVID-19 patients, without affecting short-term mortality [1].
elements.reason: The text describes the state of knowledge regarding tocilizumab in COVID-19 patients as of October 2020, noting both the evidence for reducing mechanical ventilation and the uncertainty regarding short-term mortality.

elements.quote: This report is the fi rst update of our living systematic review assessing the ef fi - cacy and safety of tocilizumab in COVID-19 patients [1].
elements.reason: The rationale for the review is explained as an update to a previous living systematic review, implying the need to incorporate new data to maintain the currency of the evidence.

elements.quote: This report is the fi rst update of our living systematic review assessing the ef fi - cacy and safety of tocilizumab in COVID-19 patients [1].
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly identifies itself as an update to a previous review (cited as [1]), explaining the need for the current review in the context of the living systematic review framework.

elements.quote: Cytokine release syndrome with elevated levels of interleukin-6 (IL-6) is associated with multiorgan damage and death in severe coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19). ... the IL-6 receptor antagonist tocilizumab reduces the risk of mechanical ventilation
elements.reason: The text describes the mechanism of action: cytokine release syndrome with elevated IL-6 is associated with damage, and tocilizumab acts as an IL-6 receptor antagonist.
The review is a standard systematic review and meta-analysis of clinical trial data; it does not involve complex interventions or delivery contexts requiring a logic model.

elements.quote: Our objective was to update the data in a living systematic review of the literature concerning the ef fi cacy and toxicity of the IL-6 receptor antagonist tocilizumab in COVID-19 patients.

elements.quote: Eligible studies were randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and observational studies at low or moderate risk of bias. The participants were hospitalized COVID-19 patients, and intervention was tocilizumab versus placebo or standard of care.

elements.quote: Eight RCTs [2 e 9], with 6311 patients, examined the effect of tocilizumab on short-term mortality (Fig. 1A); pooled RR was 0.91 (95%CI 0.72 e 1.07, I 2 25%). Seven RCTs (Fig. 1B) [2 e 7,9], with 1274 patients, examined the effect of tocilizumab on risk of mechanical ventilation

elements.quote: As several RCTs have been published since our initial review, and as per peer reviewers' and editor's recommendations, this update includes observational studies up to January 2021, and future updates will include only data from RCTs.
